title: lexindex: compact, immutable string-to-id indexes for huge catalogs
description:
Compact, immutable string-to-id indexes for huge catalogs, with a Rust core, Python bindings and a C ABI. Six complementary build-once / query-many structures: an ordered FST-backed index with prefix, range, fuzzy (Levenshtein) and subsequence queries; an ordered front-coded dictionary storing every key, which answers rank, lower-bound, prefix and range (2.64 bytes/key on real dictionary words); the same dictionary with a hash sidecar, which answers its ranks from a minimal perfect hash rather than a search; a minimal-perfect-hash dictionary with verified membership and reverse lookup; a fingerprint-based minimal-perfect-hash map storing no keys at all (1.24 bytes/key); and the bare perfect hash for a vocabulary known to be closed (0.24). A workload-aware planner prices five of them from a sample of the keys before one is built. All serialise to flat blobs, and every one but the bare perfect hash can be memory-mapped and borrowed rather than read.

Distributed on PyPI (pip install lexindex) and crates.io (cargo add lexindex); documentation at ilgrad.github.io/lexindex.
